equivalence_model.story_stripped_kernel: In a tournament on n vertices, maximize directed 3-cycles. A triple is transitive iff it has a unique top vertex; if vertex i has score w_i, the number of transitive triples is sum_i C(w_i,2). Minimize this convex sum subject to sum w_i=C(n,2), giving regular/near-regular scores.
transformations_checked: balanced cyclic schedule ↔ regular / near-regular tournament
equivalence_model.equivalence_notes: The terminology 'rock-paper-scissors triple' is simply the standard cyclic triple of tournament theory.

findings.source: Lowell W. Beineke and Frank Harary, On the Maximum Number of Cyclic Triples in Oriented Graphs, JCTB 81 (2001), 165-176
findings.relationship: Its abstract says the maximum number of cyclic triples in a tournament of given order is well known and realised by regular and near-regular tournaments.
findings.notes: This is the exact frozen extremal statistic and extremiser class.

findings.source: Classical tournament score-sequence formula (Kendall & Babington Smith / standard graph-theory texts)
findings.relationship: The number of transitive triples is sum_i C(s_i,2), yielding maxima (n^3-n)/24 for odd n and (n^3-4n)/24 for even n.
findings.notes: These are exactly the frozen formulas and proof mechanism.

classification_rationale: The candidate is the classical maximum-cyclic-triples theorem for tournaments, with the standard score-sequence proof. The round-robin/RPS wording is only a surface translation.
